Was the interview short?
Greg, do you have five minutes? The newsletter asked me for a short interview.
Five minutes, yes. After that I have a meeting. Ask your questions.
First one. When did you arrive, and how long did you travel?
I arrived on the ninth of March. Eleven hours in the air, and then four more hours on the road.
Did you sleep on the plane?
No, I didn't. I watched three movies and I read the project report twice.
Who did you meet on your first day here?
Ray, and about forty people. I forgot every name in ten minutes. I remember Ray because he gave me the wrong helmet.
Did you hear about the rain last week?
I heard about it in every e-mail. Did the water go into the lower area?
It did, on Wednesday. Last question: when was the last time you worked in a tunnel like this one?
Four years ago, in Norway. That tunnel was cold and this one is hot. Good answer? Then your five minutes are finished.

Hi Giovanna, it is Karen. You sent me five questions for the newsletter two weeks ago and I forgot to answer them. Sorry. Here they are, all five. Question one: I started in this company in two thousand nineteen, in the London office. Question two: no, I did not study engineering first. I studied geology, and I changed after three years. Question three: the last time I was on a big site was in March, in the north of England, and it rained every single day, so I know exactly how your week felt. Question four, the best thing I ever heard from a supervisor: go home, the tunnel will still be here tomorrow. And question five, the difficult one. Did I ever want to stop? Yes, once, in my first winter. I did not stop. Call me on Friday.

Good morning. Ray Collins. Before we start, three questions, and I want three short answers. Number one: who checked the pumps on Friday night? Nobody? Somebody checked them, because the lower area is dry this morning, so I want a name before lunch. Number two: did anybody call the concrete company yesterday? I asked for that call on Thursday and I did not hear anything after that. Number three, and this one is for the whole crew. Last week we lost three days. Did we learn anything, or did we only get wet? Think about it, write me one line, and give it to me on Friday. That is all. Now, the plan for today.

Last Tuesday Giovanna interviewed Greg for the site newsletter. First she asked him about the flight, and he said it took eleven hours. Then she asked who he met on his first day, and he forgot every name except one. After that she asked about the rain, and he heard about it in every e-mail. Her last question was about Norway, and that answer was the best one.
